rows.title: Delimited record service
rows.source: function solve(row){const fields=[];let field="",quoted=false;for(const ch of row){if(ch===String.fromCharCode(34))quoted=!quoted;else if(ch===","&&!quoted){fields.push(field);field="";}else field+=ch;}fields.push(field);return fields;}

Context marker: INTERVIEW-109-cb7986f69392d7ec.

The bug is in `src/core.mjs`, specifically `if(ch===String.fromCharCode(34))quoted=!quoted`: every quote only toggles state, so doubled quotes are discarded rather than decoded into one literal quote.

Smallest valid counterexample: `solve('""""')`—four quote characters, representing a quoted field containing one escaped quote. Actual: `[""]`. Required: ['"'].

Tracing those four quotes toggles `quoted` true → false → true → false; nothing is appended to `field`, so the final push produces an empty string. Four characters are minimal: an escaped quote requires two quotes inside two enclosing quotes.

automatic.answer: This is a small, dependency-free JavaScript service that parses a single valid CSV row into an array of fields. Its architecture has two layers: `src/core.mjs` exports the synchronous `solve(row)` parser, and `src/service.mjs` exposes a thin `execute(...args)` wrapper that delegates to it. Tests use Node’s built-in test runner via `npm test`; currently, they cover only a basic comma-separated row, and the parser handles quoted commas but incorrectly drops escaped double quotes instead of preserving them.

This is a dependency-free JavaScript service that parses one valid CSV row into an array of fields, preserving quoted commas and decoding doubled quotes. Its two layers are `src/core.mjs`, containing the synchronous `solve(row)` parser, and `src/service.mjs`, providing the thin `execute(...args)` wrapper. Tests run through Node’s built-in test runner with `npm test`, but currently cover only the basic `a,b` case.
